title: When Should Semantic Priors Enter Partially-Identified Causal Discovery?
abstract: arXiv:2611.14736v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Observational causal discovery often leaves causal di- rections unresolved or unstable. Large language mod- els (LLMs) can provide semantic information to resolve these directions, but incorrect proposals can exclude the true causal graph and invalidate downstream inference. We study three separate decisions: where to allocate semantic queries, which proposals to admit, and which causal graphs to retain. Our framework distinguishes population non-identifiability from finite-sample insta- bility, evaluates semantic orientation against statistical and random controls, and examines calibrated admis- sion and error-tolerant DAG retention. Experiments across benchmark networks show that semantic infor- mation improves recovery over coin-flip orientations, but targeting unstable edges has no established ad- vantage over matched-random allocation. translated_title: 语义先验应何时进入部分可识别的因果发现？
translated_abstract: 观测性因果发现常常无法确定或难以稳定地识别因果方向。大型语言模型（LLM）可以提供语义信息来解决这些方向问题，但错误的建议可能会排除真实的因果图，并使下游推断失效。我们研究了三个独立的决策：在哪里分配语义查询、采纳哪些建议以及保留哪些因果图。我们的框架区分了总体层面的不可识别性与有限样本的不稳定性，将语义定向与统计对照和随机对照进行对比评估，并考察了经校准的采纳机制和容错的DAG保留策略。在多个基准网络上的实验表明，语义信息相比抛硬币式的随机定向能改进因果结构恢复效果，但针对不稳定边进行定向相比匹配随机分配并无确证的优势。所测试的采纳证书在现有校准条件下无法支持非平凡的采纳。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个区分总体不可识别性与有限样本不稳定性的框架，系统研究语义先验（如LLM建议）应在何时、何处以何种方式进入部分可识别的因果发现，发现语义信息虽优于随机定向，但针对不稳定边并无确证优势，且现有采纳证书不足以支持非平凡的采纳。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a framework distinguishing population non-identifiability from finite-sample instability to systematically study when, where, and how semantic priors (e.g., LLM proposals) should enter partially-identified causal discovery, finding that semantic information improves recovery over random orientations but offers no established advantage when targeting unstable edges, and the tested admission certificate cannot support nontrivial admission.
